Intel Posts Strongest Revenue Growth in More Than 15 Years, with 2Q26 Revenue Reaching $16.1B  Intel reported 2Q26 revenue of $16.1B on July 23, representing 25% YoY growth and once again exceeding guidance. CEO Lip-Bu Tan described the quarter as Intel's strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years, highlighting that AI is driving unprecedented demand for computing. He added that Intel is well positioned to sustain long-term growth through its CPU portfolio, AI ASICs, advanced packaging technologies, and expanding foundry ecosystem.   hashtag #AIInferenceDemandDrives59PercentGrowthinDCAI Intel's Data Center and AI (DCAI) business generated $6.3B in revenue during the quarter, up 59% YoY, making it the company's fastest-growing business segment. Meanwhile, the Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) reported revenue of $8.9B, an increase of 13% YoY. The company partnered with SambaNova and Foxconn to showcase a production-ready, rack-scale infrastructure platform for Agentic AI inference. Additionally, Vector Core Compute (VC2) introduced a distributed agentic AI cloud solution integrating Intel Xeon processors, SambaNova RDUs, and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.   hashtag #18APEntersRiskProductionasIntelExpandsCapacity Intel Foundry reported $5.8B in revenue, up 31% YoY. On the manufacturing front, Intel 18A-P entered risk production on schedule, delivering further improvements in performance, power efficiency, and thermal characteristics. Selected Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) processors have also entered volume production using ASML's High-NA EUV (EXE) lithography platform. Intel announced a €5B investment to expand manufacturing capacity, increasing output of Intel 3-based Xeon 6 and next-generation Xeon processors. The company further expanded its custom silicon portfolio through a partnership with Fortinet to develop security processors, broadening its ASIC business beyond networking and IPUs.   hashtag #3Q26RevenueGuidedtoUS16Point8B For 3Q26, Intel expects revenue of $15.8–16.8B. CFO David Zinsner said stronger-than-expected shipments were driven by higher manufacturing yields and shorter production cycles. As AI computing demand continues to accelerate, Intel plans to significantly increase investments in manufacturing equipment, cleanroom capacity, and advanced substrates to support growth across both its product portfolio and foundry business over the next two years. Operating cash flow reached $7B during the quarter.  📊 More semiconductor insights: https://buff.ly/UWCDvd1 📊 More industry charts: https://buff.ly/4hbxzLr

【Aggressive Module House Stocking Supports NAND Spot Prices, but Rebound Momentum Remains Weak】  Overall spot market remains sluggish due to withering consumer demand. However, a certain module house, who recently saw a high visibility on enterprise SSD orders, has turned to the spot market to stock up aggressively, as suppliers are insufficient in wafers and higher in quotations. This led to a temporal halt to the depletion of spot prices. Having said that, most buyers have reached their limit of cost tolerance, aside from stocking activities among specific module houses, where order pulls from the consumer end remains on the passive end. Without support from substantial buy orders, the overall spot market still lacks momentum in price rebounds. Spot prices of 512Gb TLC wafers dropped by 1.28% this week (July 20), arriving at US$18.931.  📷 Related news from  hashtag #TrendForce: https://buff.ly/3xtxMXH 🔗 📷 For more on  hashtag #NAND Price: https://buff.ly/3VLrT2w 🔗
